SMTO-WEB-0021 — A search result snippet can't prove this fact

GUID: c47c6f92-40fe-5e6e-8796-5ffcf52c5b80
Slug: research-discovery-source-not-claim-eligible
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • The answer tried to prove a fact using only a search result preview, not the actual page. SMTO needs to read the page itself before stating the fact as checked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to read the real page or mark the fact as unconfirmed. Search previews only help find pages; the check needs the page's own text.
  2. If the run stops, ask SMTO to open the specific page and confirm the fact there, giving the web address if you know it. Reading the page itself turns the search hint into a recorded source that can prove the fact.
  3. If the run stops and an unchecked answer is acceptable to you, open the Research proof validation card shown in the run and turn off Enforce this check for this run. The answer is then shown even though this fact rests only on a search preview.

What success looks like

  • The answer shows the fact with a link to the page it came from, or clearly labels it as unverified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat a search result preview as confirmation; previews can be out of date or cut off.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof rejected a fact whose evidence span comes from a source with a role other than EVIDENCE (search discovery) or from a span marked not eligible for claims.

What this means

  • A fact relies on a source whose role is not EVIDENCE or a span marked ineligible for claims. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • A fact relies on a source whose role is not EVIDENCE or a span marked ineligible for claims.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect source role and eligible_for_claims before citing the span as verification.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_discovery_source_not_claim_eligible in _verify_fact when source.role != 'EVIDENCE' or span.eligible_for_claims is false. Acquire the primary page with Web Read (or Browser) so the fact is backed by an EVIDENCE source, or present the item as unverified; never promote a search snippet to page evidence.
  • Acquire the actual source through an authorized route, or present only the supported discovery limitation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The claim uses eligible observed evidence or clearly reports its unverified status.

What not to do

  • Do not promote a search snippet into verified page evidence.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
